notes: Pairs well with niacinamide and vitamin C for tone.

watchouts.what_to_do: Daily broad-spectrum SPF is essential — UV re-drives the pigmentation it addresses.

benefits.mechanism: Tranexamic acid inhibits plasminogen activation in keratinocytes; because UV-triggered plasmin drives release of pigment-stimulating mediators, blocking it dampens the UV-and-vascular signalling that fuels excess melanin (mechanism study vs hydroquinone, PMC5574746).
benefits.what_it_means: Visibly fades the look of stubborn, patchy discoloration (the melasma pattern) over 8-12 weeks.

benefits.mechanism: Reduced pigment-mediator signalling lowers baseline melanin deposition across the treated area (review, PMC4235096).
benefits.what_it_means: Evens overall tone and brightens with continued use.

evidence.summary: Plasmin-pathway mechanism and topical efficacy for melasma-type pigmentation shown in randomized comparisons vs hydroquinone and mechanism reviews; graded B.

citations.title: Therapeutic effects of topical tranexamic acid in comparison with hydroquinone in treatment of women with melasma
Topical tranexamic acid as a promising treatment for melasma

overview: Tranexamic acid targets the UV-and-vascular signalling that drives stubborn, patchy discoloration, making it a standout for the look of melasma-type pigmentation when paired with sun protection.

ingredient.what_it_is: A small amino-acid derivative that has become a leading topical ingredient for stubborn, UV-driven discoloration such as melasma-type patches.

marketing_vs_reality.reality: It visibly fades UV-driven discoloration with sustained use but does not erase it; melasma is recurrence-prone and daily SPF is essential to hold results.
